sources.primary_title: Microsoft to launch Saudi cloud region in November 2026
sources.verified_angle_summary: Microsoft has officially confirmed that its Saudi Arabia East datacentre region will launch in November 2026, delivering local cloud and AI infrastructure to the Kingdom. The announcement, highlighted by Ayman Alghamdi at LEAP 2026, marks a significant milestone for data residency and compliance, allowing highly regulated sectors like banking and government to transition mission-critical AI workloads to Azure. Located in the Eastern Province, the facility features three Azure Availability Zones for high availability and low latency. This development aligns with Saudi Arabia's broader digital transformation goals and is projected to generate substantial economic value and local job creation. The confirmation solidifies Microsoft's commitment to the region amid growing competition in the cloud infrastructure space.
sources.verified_key_facts: Microsoft's Saudi Arabia East cloud region will launch in November 2026; The region is located in the Eastern Province and includes three Azure Availability Zones; The infrastructure ensures local data residency for regulated sectors; The launch supports high-density AI and enterprise workloads; An IDC study estimates the region will contribute to $44 billion in new revenues for the Saudi economy between 2027 and 2030; The project is expected to create around 100,000 jobs across the Kingdom; The announcement was highlighted at LEAP 2026 by Microsoft's Ayman Alghamdi.
